proof.text: For a point x of X, Mathlib irreducibleComponent_mem_irreducibleComponents x supplies an irreducible component. The cover hypothesis supplies i : Fin 0 for that component, contradicting Fin.elim0. Thus the underlying type of X is empty.

Choose the bottom open U. Density is vacuous because X has no points. The open subscheme U is empty; Mathlib AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_of_isEmpty makes every scheme morphism into it an isomorphism, in particular the restriction of the coproduct morphism. No componentwise gluing is needed.

blueprint_update.statement: Let $X$ be a reduced scheme. Consider the empty family (indexed by the empty set) of schemes $C_i$ with morphisms $\iota_i:C_i\to X$ satisfying the component-cover hypotheses: each $C_i$ is integral, each $\iota_i$ is a closed immersion whose image is an irreducible component of $X$, distinct indices have distinct images, and every irreducible component of $X$ is the image of some $\iota_i$; and the empty family of morphisms $\nu_i:Y_i\to C_i$, each restricting to an isomorphism over a dense open subset of $C_i$. Then there is a dense open subset $U\subseteq X$ over which the morphism $\coprod_iY_i\to X$ induced by the composites $\iota_i\circ\nu_i$ (a morphism out of the empty scheme) restricts to an isomorphism.

proof.text: Let $x\in X$. The closure of the irreducible set $\{x\}$ is contained in an irreducible component $Z$ of $X$. By the cover hypothesis $Z$ is the image of some $\iota_i$, but the index set is empty, a contradiction. Hence $X$ has no points. Take $U=\varnothing$: it is dense in the empty space $X$, and the restriction of $\coprod_iY_i\to X$ over $U$ is a morphism between empty schemes, hence an isomorphism. No gluing of the components is needed.
